topic: Cold or flu? How to tell the difference

scenes.line: Cold or flu? Here are three ways to tell.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira faces camera with a curious, friendly look and gives a small wave; three numbered teal cards (1, 2, 3) stack in at the right side
scenes.animation: Hard cut in. Wave on 'Cold'. Cards pop in on 'three', 'ways', 'tell', scale 0.4 to 1.0, back.out 0.3 s each

scenes.line: One: speed. Flu comes on quickly, often within a few hours.
scenes.visual: Large '1' badge with the word 'Speed'; a teal stopwatch icon whose hand sweeps fast; a steep line labelled 'Flu' shoots upward
scenes.animation: Badge scales in on 'One', back.out 0.3 s; stopwatch hand spins one turn on 'quickly', power2.out; steep line draws on 'hours', power2.out 0.4 s

scenes.visual: Same chart: a second, gentle orange line labelled 'Cold' rises slowly next to the steep teal flu line
scenes.animation: Gentle line draws left to right from 'creeps' to 'gradually', power1.inOut 1.4 s

scenes.line: Two: where you feel it. A cold mainly affects your nose and throat.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, relaxed and explaining, open-palm gesture; a '2' badge at upper left and a simple head-profile icon with the nose and throat highlighted in soft teal at the side
scenes.animation: Badge pops in on 'Two', back.out 0.3 s; nose highlight fades in on 'nose', throat highlight on 'throat', 0.3 s each

scenes.line: Flu hits more than that, with body aches, a high temperature and exhaustion.
scenes.visual: Three rounded white cards side by side: an aching body outline, a thermometer, a low battery; header 'Flu goes further:'
scenes.animation: Header fades in on 'Flu'; cards slide up one by one on 'aches', 'temperature', 'exhaustion', power2.out 0.35 s

scenes.line: Three: how you cope. With a cold, you can usually carry on as normal.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, easy smile, nods; a '3' badge at upper left and a small briefcase card with a teal tick at the side
scenes.animation: Badge pops in on 'Three', back.out 0.3 s; briefcase card slides in on 'carry', tick draws on 'normal'

scenes.line: Flu can leave you too exhausted to carry on.
scenes.visual: Simple bed outline with a pillow and blanket on a cream card, a low battery icon above it
scenes.animation: Bed card rises in on 'Flu', power2.out 0.35 s; battery bar drains from full to one bar on 'exhausted', power1.inOut 0.8 s

scenes.line: Either way, rest and drink plenty of water, and stay home if you have a high temperature.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, warm and reassuring, gives a gentle wave toward the cards; three small cards appear at the side: bed, water glass, house
scenes.animation: Cards pop in on 'rest', 'water', 'home', scale 0 to 1, back.out 0.3 s each

scenes.line: If flu symptoms do not improve after seven days,
scenes.visual: A week calendar with seven day squares filling in teal one by one, a '7 days' label beneath
scenes.animation: Day squares fill left to right from 'symptoms' to 'seven', stagger 0.15 s; label pops on 'days'

scenes.line: or you feel short of breath, talk to a doctor.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, calm and direct, open-palm gesture; a lungs outline card and a stethoscope card appear at the sides
scenes.animation: Lungs card fades in on 'breath', stethoscope card slides in on 'doctor', power2.out 0.3 s

scenes.line: Save this for the next time you feel rough.
scenes.visual: Dr. Ira, friendly smile, waves; a bookmark icon at upper right
scenes.animation: Bookmark bounces on 'Save', scale 0.8 to 1.1 to 1.0, back.out; wave on 'next'

scenes.visual: Cream end card with Pulse Health wordmark centred
